# Rick Jackson Watchdog File

Subject: Rick Jackson, Republican nominee for Governor of Georgia, 2026
Compiled: October 23, 2026 for the On Point Politics watchdog database, onpointpolitics.us
Data cutoff: October 22, 2026. The latest filed Georgia figures run through July 31, 2026.
Next scheduled data drop: the Georgia report covering activity through October 20, 2026, due the week of October 26 according to the AJC. The exact due date was not verified.

## Bottom line up front

1. Rick Jackson is mostly his own donor. He spent more than $108 million of his own fortune to win the nomination through June 2026, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/), and his campaign accounts had raised roughly $130 million through July 31, much of it his own money, per the [AJC on October 21](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/). Analysts expect about $200 million by Election Day. That is an estimate, not a filing.
2. His own company is the largest interest in the file. Jackson Healthcare subsidiaries have received more than $1 billion in payments from Georgia agencies since 2020 and more than $56 million in 2025 alone from Behavioral Health, Community Health and Corrections, per the [AJC on March 5, 2026](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/rick-jackson-promises-to-unwind-his-companys-state-contracts-if-elected/). The governor appoints the people who run those agencies.
3. The Republican Governors Association gave $10 million to his new leadership committee, For All Georgians Inc., about two weeks after he opened it in June 2026, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/) and the [Georgia Recorder](https://cobbcountycourier.com/2026/08/gop-candidates-outraise-democrats-so-far-in-most-but-not-all-of-georgias-statewide-contests/). Months earlier he had sued to stop his primary rival from using the same kind of committee.
4. A live federal tax fight. The IRS says about $54 million in Jackson deductions tied to film investments were improper and assessed $16 million in penalties. Jackson is disputing both in U.S. Tax Court, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-and-her-husband-have-a-history-of-late-tax-payments/). He has no public position on the Georgia film tax credit in the sources read.
5. Trump world. He gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. about a month before launching in February 2026, per [CNN via ABC17](https://abc17news.com/?p=1624327), and has promised to be Trump's "favorite governor."

## Committee structure and treasurer

Jackson runs a capped Georgia candidate committee and an unlimited leadership committee, For All Georgians Inc., which he opened after winning the June 16, 2026 runoff over Lt. Gov. Burt Jones. Georgia's 2021 law lets the governor, the lieutenant governor, the two parties' nominees for those offices and legislative leaders run leadership committees that take unlimited gifts and coordinate with campaigns, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/how-georgias-unlimited-money-machine-is-powering-the-governors-race/) and [GPB](https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/02/24/judge-rules-against-burt-jones-unlimited-fundraising-in-race-for-georgia-governor). For All Georgians transferred $5 million to the campaign committee in the June 11 to July 31 period, per [Capitol Beat](https://roughdraftatlanta.com/2026/08/11/rick-jackson-outpaces-bottoms-fundraising/). The campaign reported $4.3 million cash at the end of July, while the AJC put cash across all his accounts at roughly $11 million.

The treasurer, the state filer IDs and any compliance firm were not found. The Georgia Government Transparency and Campaign Finance Commission site refused automated access, so no filing was read directly. Spokespeople on record include Garrison Douglas, Dave Abrams and Mike Schrimpf. Schrimpf was also paid $90,000 in consulting fees.

## Self funding

Documented. Jackson pledged at least $50 million at his February 4, 2026 launch, per the [AJC](https://feeds.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/republican-outsiders-50m-bet-remakes-georgia-governors-race). By July 2 he had given more than $111 million and his campaign had spent more than $108 million, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/). After the nomination he put in no new cash or loans through July 31, only tens of thousands in kind for legal fees, rent and travel, per [Capitol Beat](https://roughdraftatlanta.com/2026/08/11/rick-jackson-outpaces-bottoms-fundraising/). AdImpact counted $102 million in ad reservations this year and an $87 million general election buy, per the AJC. His ad line: "I'll spend whatever it takes to win this race." He told WJCL "I can't be bought."

Money out through July 2: Smart Media Group of Alexandria, Virginia, more than $62 million in TV and cable plus $750,000 radio; Ballast, more than $18 million; GMRP, roughly $14 million, mostly mail; Quiver, roughly $5.7 million; polling about $2.7 million to unnamed vendors; legal about $500,000, mostly Kilpatrick Townsend & Stockton; Crosby Ottenhoff Group about $200,000; AJ Strategies more than $125,000; Michael Schrimpf $90,000; Robinson Republic about $50,000. Staff salaries were only about $209,000.

Inference: a candidate who funds himself owes few donors, which is his own argument. The flip side is that the one interest with the most money riding on the governor's office is his own company, covered next.

## Health care and pharma: Jackson Healthcare and the state

Documented. Jackson owns and runs Jackson Healthcare of Alpharetta, which reports more than $3 billion a year in income. Its subsidiaries Healthcare Workforce Logistics, Jackson & Coker and LocumTenens have taken more than $1 billion in Georgia agency payments since a 2020 COVID staffing contract that was awarded without bids under the public health emergency, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/rick-jackson-promises-to-unwind-his-companys-state-contracts-if-elected/). In 2025 the payments topped $56 million from Behavioral Health, Community Health and Corrections. He also bought a Tennessee antibiotics plant in 2021, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/why-rick-jackson-says-hell-be-trumps-favorite-governor/).

The lever. The governor appoints the commissioners of those three departments. Community Health runs Medicaid. A bill to bar people with state business from statewide office stalled when Speaker Jon Burns declined to call it in March 2026, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/6-takeaways-from-a-hectic-crossover-day-in-the-georgia-legislature/).

What he has said. His campaign said on March 5 that the company "will not bid on any new contracts with the state of Georgia" and will "work to responsibly unwind any existing contracts." Jackson said "Whatever the law says we're going to do, we're going to do." His campaign says he has pledged to give 100 percent of his net worth to charity. No blind trust or divestiture pledge was found. Jones called the company the "culprit" in rising costs; the Jackson camp called that a "meltdown." Jackson opposes Medicaid expansion and backs a "state solution" to cut middlemen.

Inference: "unwind" has no published timetable, no named contracts and no independent monitor. Whoever runs Behavioral Health, Community Health and Corrections in 2027 will be a Jackson appointee deciding whether and how fast his company's state revenue winds down.

## Party and leadership: the RGA and For All Georgians

Documented. The RGA gave $10 million to For All Georgians in June 2026. Other six figure checks to the committee were $100,000 each from Ben Tarbutton, Evans General Contractors and Curae Finance, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/). In February Jackson sued Jones, Attorney General Chris Carr and Ethics Commission members in federal court, arguing the leadership committee law gave Jones "his own rulebook." Judge Thomas Thrash issued a restraining order on February 20, then ruled against Jones on March 13 but stayed the ruling, per [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/gop-candidate-for-georgia-governor-wins-temporary-restraining-order-against-lt-gov-burt-jones-leadership-committee/) and the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/judge-lets-burt-jones-committee-continue-to-spend-on-his-campaign-for-now/).

Inference: Jackson attacked the unlimited committee as unfair when he could not have one and adopted it once he could. The RGA's own top funders were not traced in this pass.

## Trump world

Documented. Jackson gave $1 million to MAGA Inc. about a month before launching, per [CNN via ABC17](https://abc17news.com/?p=1624327), which Jones called an "11th hour MAGA embrace," per the AJC. Jones also said Jackson gave to Trump's GOP rivals for most of the past decade. Trump and Gov. Kemp endorsed Jones. Jackson pledged on immigration: "We will support the feds with whatever they want."

## Own finances and disclosure history

Jackson reported a $3 billion net worth on state disclosures, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/). The disclosure form itself was not read. The IRS film deduction dispute is pending in Tax Court. The case number and filing dates were not found.

## Enforcement and controversies

Georgians for Integrity, an anonymous Delaware nonprofit with an East Atlanta mail drop, spent about $20 million attacking Jones, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/06/rick-jackson-topples-burt-jones-wins-gop-nod-for-governor/). The Georgia GOP filed an ethics complaint seeking donor disclosure, per the [AJC](https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/01/an-8m-mystery-triggers-growing-fight-over-dark-money-in-georgia-politics/). Jones allies suspected Jackson. Jackson has repeatedly denied any connection, and no filing links him. Status contested.

Tax Court. Allegation: the IRS says $54 million in film investment deductions were improper. Response: Jackson is contesting it in court. The Bottoms campaign says he "owes $54 million in federal taxes and $16 million in penalties," which overstates what the AJC reports.

Defamation suit. Jackson sued Jones in March 2026 over campaign statements. The Jones campaign said "Rick Jackson's thin skin is showing." No outcome was found.

National Guard. Bottoms said on October 6 that Jackson promised to send the National Guard during the election. Jackson called it "a complete falsehood," per [Atlanta News First](https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/video/2026/10/07/bottoms-says-jackson-promises-send-national-guard-during-election/).

## Deal table

| Interest | Money in | Ask | Lever | Stake | Decision date |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jackson Healthcare | Owner; $108M plus self funding | Orderly or slow unwind of state contracts | Appoints heads of Behavioral Health, Community Health, Corrections | More than $1B since 2020; $56M plus in 2025 | January 2027 onward |
| Republican Governors Association | $10M to For All Georgians, June 2026 | Hold the seat; national party priorities | Governor's agenda, appointments | Not quantified | November 3, 2026 |
| Trump world | Jackson gave $1M to MAGA Inc. | Full cooperation on immigration enforcement | State police and Guard posture, agency directives | Not quantified | January 2027 onward |
| Construction and finance donors | $100K each from Evans General Contractors, Curae Finance, Ben Tarbutton | Not stated | Budget, tax cuts, contracts | Not quantified | 2027 session |
| Film investments | Jackson's own | Credit posture | Signs or vetoes film credit changes | $54M in disputed deductions | 2027 or 2028 session |

## Levers and calendar

| Decision | Who holds it now | When | Donors who care |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jackson Healthcare state contracts | Kemp appointees | January 2027 on | Jackson |
| Medicaid expansion versus Pathways | Governor, DCH, legislature | 2027 session | Health care |
| State contractor eligibility bill | House Speaker | 2027 session | Jackson |
| Leadership committee law | Legislature, federal court | Pending | RGA |
| Income tax cut in half, property tax freeze | Governor, legislature | 2027 session | Business donors |
| Data center siting and cost shift | PSC, legislature | 2027 session | None documented |

Calendar: November 3, 2026 general election, with a runoff possible if no one tops 50 percent; the runoff date was not verified. The pre-general report lands the week of October 26. The governor takes office in January 2027 and the 2027 session follows. The Tax Court case and the leadership committee case have no dates in the sources read. The 2028 session is the next window for film credit or contractor law changes.

## What we could not verify

The Georgia Ethics Commission site, ethics.ga.gov, refused automated fetches, so no Georgia filing was read: committee IDs, treasurer, October receipts and the disclosure form are missing. Not read: wikipedia.org on Jackson, blocked; the Jones Facebook post on the 2013 Abrams gift; Bluestein posts on X about the $3B net worth; legis.ga.gov bill 73340, which did not load; and the pending AJC report on the October filing. The 2013 Abrams gift is a Jones campaign claim only. RGA funders, Evans General Contractors state contracts, Ben Tarbutton's and Curae Finance's business lines, and the Tax Court docket were not traced. The Jackson Healthcare payment totals come only from AJC analysis, not from state payment records.

# Rick Jackson research notes

Compiled October 23, 2026. About 45 tool calls across both Georgia subjects. The shared web search budget ran out partway through, so later work used only WebFetch on URLs already surfaced and on AJC section and article pages linked from those. No Georgia filing was read: ethics.ga.gov refused fetches on robots grounds, transparencyusa.org/ga shows only 2022 cycle data, and api.usaspending.gov was blocked at the proxy.

## Thread 1: Committees and IDs

### Takeaway
Two vehicles: the candidate committee and For All Georgians Inc., a leadership committee opened in June 2026 after the runoff win. Treasurer and filer IDs are not found.

### Cited findings
- For All Georgians Inc. named as his leadership committee, created under the 2021 law; RGA gave it $10 million. Georgia Recorder via Cobb Courier, Aug 12 2026: https://cobbcountycourier.com/2026/08/gop-candidates-outraise-democrats-so-far-in-most-but-not-all-of-georgias-statewide-contests/
- Committee opened in June after the nomination; RGA check came about two weeks later. AJC Aug 8 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/08/georgia-governor-race-rick-jackson-raises-13m-in-outside-money/
- For All Georgians Inc. gave the campaign $5 million; campaign raised $6.1M in the Jun 11 to Jul 31 period; $4.3M cash end of July; more than $118M raised or given overall; corporate gifts over $240,000; nearly $200,000 from outside Georgia. Capitol Beat Aug 11 2026: https://roughdraftatlanta.com/2026/08/11/rick-jackson-outpaces-bottoms-fundraising/ ; also republished at https://www.mainstreetnews.com/jackson/state_news/jackson-leads-bottoms-in-fundraising-for-georgia-governors-race/article_fa62134f-505d-4354-86ce-09398e50fabd.html , which is the same reporting and not an independent source.
- Leadership committee law: 2021, available to governor, lieutenant governor, the nominees for those offices and legislative leaders; unlimited gifts; can raise during session. AJC Feb 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/how-georgias-unlimited-money-machine-is-powering-the-governors-race/ and GPB Feb 24 2026: https://www.gpb.org/news/2026/02/24/judge-rules-against-burt-jones-unlimited-fundraising-in-race-for-georgia-governor
- Spokespeople: Garrison Douglas per Georgia Recorder; Dave Abrams per CBS and GPB; Mike Schrimpf per AJC Mar 5 2026.

### Inferences
Inference: AJC's roughly $11 million cash figure and Capitol Beat's $4.3 million differ because AJC counts both accounts.

### Gaps
Treasurer, compliance firm, state filer IDs, For All Georgians full donor list.

## Thread 2: Money in

### Takeaway
Self funding dominates. Outside money after the nomination is mostly the RGA's $10 million.

### Cited findings
- More than $108M spent and more than $111M given by Jackson as of Jul 2 2026; vendor breakdown. AJC Jul 2 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/07/heres-how-rick-jackson-spent-108-million-in-the-republican-race-for-governor/
- No new loans or cash after nomination; about $13M raised across accounts Jun 11 to Jul 31; $87M ad buy; $102M AdImpact reservations; six figure gifts of $100,000 each from Ben Tarbutton, Evans General Contractors, Curae Finance. AJC Aug 8 2026, link above.
- Roughly $130M raised through end of July, much of it his own; analysts project about $200M. AJC Oct 21 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/pritzker-bloomberg-donate-keisha-lance-bottoms-georgia-governor/
- More than $100M by the runoff; $90M on ads per AdImpact; initially committed $50M; $1M to MAGA Inc. about a month before launch. CNN via ABC17, Jun 16 2026: https://abc17news.com/?p=1624327 and KRDO: https://krdo.com/?p=1733670
- Pledge of at least $50M at the Feb 4 launch. AJC: https://feeds.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/republican-outsiders-50m-bet-remakes-georgia-governors-race
- Over $80M in by May 21. AJC opinion column, Patricia Murphy: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/05/how-much-for-that-georgia-governors-mansion/
- CRE donors: Allman $21,600; Tyndall $4,800 June; Bolton $4,000 May; Meyer $2,000 July; Perry $2,000 July; at least $67K total. Bisnow Aug 16 2026: https://www.bisnow.com/news/atlanta/economic-development/jackson-far-outraising-bottoms-georgia-governor-race-cre-execs-donations-campaign-finance
- Sept 30 Buckhead gala with $15,000 host spots and up to $100,000 VIP reception. AJC Sept 17 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/09/can-keisha-lance-bottoms-withstand-rick-jacksons-spending-blitz-in-georgia/
- Pro-Jackson spending or reservations of nearly $76M for the general per AdImpact, same AJC Sept 17 article.

### Inferences
Inference: the Sept 30 gala and the RGA check mean the October report should show more outside money than the July report did. Treat as unconfirmed until filed.

### Gaps
August to October receipts; RGA's own funders; businesses of Tarbutton and Curae Finance.

## Thread 3: Money out

### Takeaway
Smart Media Group is the dominant vendor. Pollsters are unnamed.

### Cited findings
Smart Media Group more than $62M TV and cable plus $750,000 radio; Ballast more than $18M; GMRP about $14M; Quiver about $5.7M; polling about $2.7M; phone banks about $2.1M; staff about $209,000; legal about $500,000 mostly Kilpatrick Townsend & Stockton; Crosby Ottenhoff about $200,000; AJ Strategies more than $125,000; Michael Schrimpf $90,000; Robinson Republic about $50,000. AJC Jul 2 2026, link above. Over $50,000 for helicopter and plane, nearly $35,000 legal, post nomination, Georgia Recorder link above.

### Inferences
Inference: Smart Media Group of Alexandria, Virginia is a national GOP media buyer; its other clients were not checked.

### Gaps
Pollster names; general election vendor totals; any payments to Jackson Healthcare or Jackson entities for rent, which Capitol Beat says were in kind.

## Thread 4: Own finances

### Takeaway
$3 billion net worth on disclosures; IRS film deduction dispute in Tax Court; owns Jackson Healthcare and a Tennessee antibiotics plant.

### Cited findings
- $3B on state disclosures. AJC Jul 2 2026 and AJC Jun 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/06/rick-jackson-topples-burt-jones-wins-gop-nod-for-governor/
- IRS says about $54M in film investment deductions improper, $16M penalties, disputed in Tax Court. AJC Oct 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/10/keisha-lance-bottoms-and-her-husband-have-a-history-of-late-tax-payments/
- Company reports more than $3B a year in income; pledge to give 100 percent of net worth to charity. AJC Mar 5 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/rick-jackson-promises-to-unwind-his-companys-state-contracts-if-elected/
- 2021 purchase of a Tennessee antibiotics plant. AJC Feb 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/02/why-rick-jackson-says-hell-be-trumps-favorite-governor/

### Inferences
Inference: the film deduction dispute is a federal matter, but it makes his silence on Georgia's film tax credit a live question.

### Gaps
Disclosure form; Tax Court docket; plant name; film investment vehicles.

## Thread 5: Enforcement and controversies

### Takeaway
He is the plaintiff in two suits against Jones and the suspected but denying beneficiary of a $20M dark money campaign.

### Cited findings
- TRO Feb 20 2026, Judge Thrash, against WBJ Leadership Committee; ads since Feb 10 canceled. CBS: https://www.cbsnews.com/atlanta/news/gop-candidate-for-georgia-governor-wins-temporary-restraining-order-against-lt-gov-burt-jones-leadership-committee/ ; GPB link above; WBJ had $15.9M Jan 31.
- Mar 13 2026 ruling against Jones stayed; contempt motion pending. AJC: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/judge-lets-burt-jones-committee-continue-to-spend-on-his-campaign-for-now/
- Defamation suit Mar 2026; Jones campaign response. AJC: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/rick-jackson-sues-burt-jones-for-defamation-amid-heated-governors-race/
- Georgians for Integrity: about $8M by Jan 2 2026, Delaware nonprofit, East Atlanta mail drop, GOP ethics complaint, lawyer James Tyrrell III. AJC: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/01/an-8m-mystery-triggers-growing-fight-over-dark-money-in-georgia-politics/ ; about $14M and Jackson aide denial, AJC Feb link above; $19M and repeated denials, AJC Mar: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/how-the-jones-jackson-clash-has-engulfed-the-governors-race-and-georgia-politics/ ; $20M, AJC Jun link above.
- National Guard claim and denial. Atlanta News First Oct 6 2026: https://www.atlantanewsfirst.com/video/2026/10/07/bottoms-says-jackson-promises-send-national-guard-during-election/
- 2013 company gift to Stacey Abrams, Jones campaign claim. AJC May 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/05/after-costly-primary-burt-jones-plans-to-use-rick-jacksons-wealth-against-him/

### Inferences
Inference: no filing ties Jackson to Georgians for Integrity; storing it as Contested is the ceiling.

### Gaps
Outcome of the GOP ethics complaint; contempt motion ruling; defamation suit court and outcome; any 11th Circuit appeal.

## Thread 6: Hop two

### Takeaway
The strongest hop two chain is the state's payments to his own company.

### Cited findings
State agencies to Jackson Healthcare subsidiaries more than $1B since 2020 and more than $56M in 2025, AJC Mar 5 2026 link above. Contractor eligibility bill stalled. AJC Mar 9 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/03/6-takeaways-from-a-hectic-crossover-day-in-the-georgia-legislature/ . The AJC Mar 5 article names it House Bill 1362 and gives the 3 percent and 25 percent ownership tests; legis.ga.gov bill page did not load: https://www.legis.ga.gov/legislation/73340 . Egbert Perry gave to both nominees, Bisnow link above.

### Inferences
Inference: RGA, Evans General Contractors and Curae Finance second hops could not be traced without search.

### Gaps
RGA donors; Evans General Contractors state work; lobbyists for any donor.

## Thread 7: Levers

### Takeaway
Agency appointments over his own company's contracts, Medicaid expansion, taxes, data centers, immigration.

### Cited findings
Opposes Medicaid expansion; halve income tax; freeze property taxes; "support the feds with whatever they want"; six-week law unchanged. AJC Feb 2026 link above. Data centers: guardrails, communities decide. AJC Oct 22 2026: https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/10/poll-georgians-government-regulation-of-ai/ . Unwind pledge, AJC Mar 5 link above.

### Inferences
Inference: the unwind pledge lacks a timetable or monitor.

### Gaps
Positions on PSC appointments, film tax credit, Georgia Promise Scholarship.

## Thread 8: Votes and record

### Takeaway
Never held office. No votes. The record is the company's contracts and his 2020 pandemic role.

### Cited findings
Never held elected office. AJC Jun 2026: https://www.ajc.com/politics/2026/06/keisha-lance-bottoms-is-in-for-a-very-different-race-against-rick-jackson/ . Involved in foster care legislation and pandemic response, AJC Feb 2026 link above.

### Inferences
None.

### Gaps
Specific foster care bills he backed; any state board appointments he held.
